coverage_goals: Loop body executes exactly 16 times for all test cases
Both return paths (match and mismatch) are exercised
All byte positions are tested as mismatch locations
Accumulator variable transitions through intermediate states
mutation_goals: Insert early return after first mismatch detection (should fail timing test)
Replace bitwise OR with logical OR in accumulation (should fail timing test)
Add if-else branch on intermediate comparison result (should fail static analysis)
Change loop bound from constant 16 to variable (should fail static analysis)
Use ternary operator with comparison-dependent condition (should fail static analysis)
negative_tests: First byte mismatch: input[0] differs, remaining 15 bytes match
Last byte mismatch: input[15] differs, first 15 bytes match
Middle byte mismatch: input[8] differs, other bytes match
Multiple byte mismatches: input differs at positions 3, 7, 12
All bytes mismatch: input and reference completely different
positive_tests: All 16 bytes match: input and reference tokens identical
Random matching tokens: generate 10 random 16-byte values, use same value for both input and reference
Boundary values: tokens with all 0x00, all 0xFF, alternating 0xAA/0x55 patterns

forbidden_patterns: return statement inside comparison loop body
break or continue statements dependent on comparison results
short-circuit logical operators (&&, ||) applied to byte comparison results
if-else branches where condition depends on intermediate comparison state
variable loop bounds that depend on token content
ternary operator (? :) with secret-dependent condition inside loop
early exit from function before processing all 16 bytes
hidden_spec.oracle_notes: The oracle must verify constant-time execution through both static analysis and dynamic simulation. Static checks include: (1) no return/break/continue inside the loop, (2) no if-else with comparison-derived conditions, (3) no short-circuit operators on comparison results. Dynamic checks include: (4) RTL simulation measuring cycle counts for edge cases (all match, first byte mismatch, middle byte mismatch, last byte mismatch, all mismatch), (5) verification that cycle count variance is zero across all test cases. The correct implementation pattern uses bitwise OR or AND accumulation of XOR results without branching. Example: result = 1; for(i=0; i<16; i++) { result &= (input_token[i] == reference_token[i]); } or using XOR accumulation: diff = 0; for(i=0; i<16; i++) { diff |= (input_token[i] ^ reference_token[i]); } return (diff == 0);

security_requirements.detection_strategy: RTL simulation measuring cycle count for multiple input patterns including all-match, first-byte-mismatch, last-byte-mismatch, and random mismatches; verify identical cycle counts
security_requirements.requirement: Execution latency must be constant and independent of input token values

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: grep for 'return' statements inside loop body; AST analysis to detect break/continue statements
security_requirements.requirement: No early termination or return statement inside the comparison loop

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Simulation with instrumentation counting loop iterations; verify count equals 16 for all test vectors
security_requirements.requirement: Loop iteration count must be exactly 16 for all inputs

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: detect if-else or ternary operators with conditions derived from byte comparison results; CFG analysis for data-dependent branches
security_requirements.requirement: No secret-dependent conditional branches that affect control flow

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Code review for logical AND/OR operators applied to comparison results; verify bitwise operations used instead
security_requirements.requirement: Comparison result must be accumulated without short-circuit evaluation

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker has access to precise timing measurements of the compare_token function execution. By providing crafted input tokens and measuring execution time, the attacker attempts to infer information about the reference token value. A timing difference when the first byte mismatches versus when the last byte mismatches reveals the position of the first differing byte, enabling byte-by-byte token recovery through binary search. The attacker model assumes the reference token is secret (e.g., authentication key, MAC tag) and the input token is attacker-controlled. The hardware implementation must prevent timing-based information leakage by ensuring constant execution time regardless of where or whether a mismatch occurs.

constraints: No dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, realloc, free)
All loops must have compile-time determinable bounds
Maximum function size: 50 lines of C code
Must be synthesizable by PandA-Bambu to RTL
Use only standard C99 with stdint.h types
public_spec.description: Implement a hardware-synthesizable C function that compares a 16-byte input token against a 16-byte reference token. The function must return 1 if the tokens match exactly, or 0 if they differ. The implementation must be suitable for synthesis with PandA-Bambu and execute the comparison for all 16 bytes regardless of intermediate results.

functional_requirements.requirement: The function must compare all 16 bytes of input_token against reference_token
Return value must be 1 if and only if all 16 bytes match exactly
Return value must be 0 if any byte position differs
The function must process the entire 16-byte length for every invocation
Use only standard C99 integer types from stdint.h (uint8_t, uint16_t, uint32_t, uint64_t)

public_spec.interface:
uint8_t compare_token(const uint8_t input_token[16], const uint8_t reference_token[16])

Parameters:
- input_token: pointer to 16-byte array containing the token to verify
- reference_token: pointer to 16-byte array containing the expected token value

Returns:
- 1 if all 16 bytes match
- 0 if any byte differs
